dedupe_keys.name: ecologistics tool for urban freight co2 accounting and decarbonisation scenarios

description: The EcoLogistics tool is a collaborative decision support system that helps city governments track greenhouse gas emissions from urban freight and test decarbonisation measures. It is described by Beatriz Royo, Yiqian Zhang, Alan Lewis and Payam Dehdari of the Zaragoza Logistics Center, ICLEI - Local Governments for Sustainability and Stuttgart Technical University of Applied Sciences (Case Studies on Transport Policy, 2025). Coverage: urban freight carbon accounting that harmonises GHG protocols for cities with the GLEC Framework, demonstrated in Bogotá, where city officials assessed 2019 CO2-equivalent emissions and explored electrification scenarios for 2030 and 2050; the results fed a low-carbon urban freight action plan focused on fleet electrification. The authors present it as applicable to cities in any economic or logistics context. Format and access: an open access article describing the tool. Licence and cost: the article is free under CC BY-NC-ND; how the tool itself is distributed is not stated in the abstract. Caveats: one city case study; city data gaps limit accuracy. The inventory and scenario logic can be used to turn simulated urban freight flows into emissions for policy comparison. It relates to EcoTransIT World and COPERT in the catalogue.
